calls.purpose: Baseline for paired comparisons and source of loop examples: the unedited model under the evaluation decoding (T=0.8, top-k 40) on dev prompts 0-63, seed 0. Hypothesis: loops are re-uses of earlier 4-grams of the same story (copying from context), not token stutter.

Which heads copy from context. Hypothesis: a few late-layer heads (weights-only candidates L4H6, L5H6, L5H0, L5H7) attend to the token that followed the previous occurrence of the current token and write that token's logit; their direct logit contribution to the true next token is much larger at positions that complete an already-seen n-gram than elsewhere, on model generations and on real stories. Second hypothesis: the model's probability of repeating an n-gram is calibrated on real stories at T=1, so the excess repetition comes from sharpened decoding of a copy signal, not from a mis-trained component.
Baseline loss on dev stories 1-64 (<eot>+story, cut at 256 tokens), the reference for every paired loss comparison of an ablation or an edit.

Hypothesis: heads L5H6, L5H7, L5H1, L4H5 carry the in-context copying that produces repeated 4-grams. Prediction: with their output zeroed, loop rate and rep-4 on prompts 0-63 seed 0 fall far below the unedited model's 0.234 / 0.0255 (pass 1).

Same hypothesis, cost side: how much of the loss on real stories depends on the four copy heads. Prediction: zeroing them raises loss well above the 0.02 tolerance, i.e. copying is useful and cannot simply be removed.

Control for the copy-head hypothesis: zeroing four heads of the same layers without copy signatures (L5H0, L5H2, L5H3, L4H1). Prediction: loop rate and rep-4 do not fall as they do for the copy heads.
Control, cost side: loss change from zeroing the four non-copy heads, to compare with the copy heads' cost.
